curriculum.lesson_evidence: Passing and moving is a team strategy: after you pass, move into an open space so you can receive the ball again. This keeps the ball moving, makes defenders move and helps the team keep possession. Use clear communication ('Here!') and pass to open teammates, not just to friends. Keep the game safe with no contact, soft balls and enough space.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A player passes the ball and then stands still. Describe what the player should do next and why.

FEEDBACK
They should move into an open space and call 'Here!' so they are available for the next pass. Moving after passing keeps the ball moving and gives teammates more options.

WATCH FOR
Thinking the person who passes has finished their job. Moving to a new space keeps them part of the play.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Set up a small passing game for 3 or 4 players (3 versus 1 works well). Practise 'pass and move' for 3 rounds. Record the longest run of passes and describe where players moved to get open.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: in a 3 versus 1 passing game, Eli passes to Ava and then runs into an empty space on the left. Ava passes back to Eli in the space, and they keep the ball for 8 passes. The defender cannot intercept because the ball keeps moving to open players.

TRY FIRST
A player passes the ball and then stands still. Describe what the player should do next and why.

FEEDBACK
They should move into an open space and call 'Here!' so they are available for the next pass. Moving after passing keeps the ball moving and gives teammates more options.
teach_steps.explain:
Passing and moving is a team strategy: after you pass, move into an open space so you can receive the ball again. This keeps the ball moving, makes defenders move and helps the team keep possession. Use clear communication ('Here!') and pass to open teammates, not just to friends. Keep the game safe with no contact, soft balls and enough space.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.
